title: Adapter revision lifecycle
summary: How an adapter goes from a saved draft to devices that store readings. The second row deploys a tested revision into the tenant runtime. The third row runs right to left: the adapter's births become discovered sources, a person activates one, and the runtime applies the device's configuration. Activation deploys the same revision again so the publisher knows the new binding.

boxes.label: Draft saved
boxes.sub: Every save is a new revision
boxes.detail: A save stores the decoder, fixtures, source settings and the pinned profile revision as an immutable revision with a content hash and a snapshot of the secrets. It is refused when the draft changed underneath (409) or while a deployment is pending.

boxes.label: Decoder tests
boxes.detail: adapter-manager runs the revision's decoder on its fixtures with the limits the tenant runtime uses, and validates each output against the profile. The result is stored on that exact revision; only a revision whose tests passed can be deployed.

boxes.label: Deploy requested
boxes.detail: Creates an operation (`deploy`, `pause` or `rollback`) keyed by the request's UUID, so a retried request returns the same one. The adapter's desired revision is set and its status becomes `pending`; a second request is refused until this one finishes.

boxes.label: device-adapters worker
boxes.detail: A queue worker of its own. The job claims the queued operation, drops it if a newer request superseded it, ensures the adapter has a Sparkplug gateway with broker credentials, tests a vendor broker connection, and sends the revision with its secrets, profile and device bindings to adapter-manager.

boxes.label: adapter-manager
boxes.detail: Serializes work per tenant. It makes sure the tenant's two containers exist (ingress broker and Node-RED runtime, with memory and CPU limits), provisions the adapter's broker identities and builds the adapter's flow from the request.

boxes.label: Deployment failed
boxes.detail: Any error or a timeout marks the operation and the adapter `failed` with a diagnostic. Nothing is retried automatically: the job has one attempt and 180 seconds. A person inspects runtime health and deploys again.

boxes.label: Tenant Node-RED
boxes.detail: The manager replaces only this adapter's tab through the admin API, then reads the flows back and checks that the publisher node carries the requested revision. A pause removes the tab. The editor is disabled; flows change only this way.

boxes.label: Publisher announces
boxes.detail: The new publisher connects to the platform broker and sends NBIRTH and a DBIRTH for every source in the adapter's births file, so a redeploy does not leave known sources unannounced. New sources get their DBIRTH with their first decoded payload.

boxes.label: Discovered source
boxes.detail: Two records meet here. The reporter's sample creates the adapter's candidate with a preview. The runtime's `discovery.birth.v1` event stores the birth's metric names and datatypes on a Discovery candidate under the adapter's gateway, and raises its birth revision when they change.

boxes.label: Activate device
boxes.detail: Needs a running adapter and a birth seen by the runtime. In one transaction it creates the installation that ties the source to a device, maps every reporting profile parameter to the metric of the same key, requests the device's activation and queues a deploy of the applied revision.

boxes.label: Runtime applies
boxes.detail: The runtime checks the configuration against the source's live birth. An adapter-fed source that has no live birth is checked against the `birth_metrics` Laravel sent. On success the request's generation becomes the device's applied generation, which telemetry and automation bindings use. A refusal leaves it unchanged.

boxes.label: Review required
boxes.detail: When a later birth does not fit the applied configuration, the device stays online with a diagnostic and its readings stop being mapped. A birth that fits again clears the review by itself; otherwise a person activates a new configuration.

steps.text: Someone saves the adapter. The save is a new immutable revision; the decoder tests then run on its fixtures and the result is stored on it.
Deploying the tested revision creates a queued operation and sets the adapter to pending. Rollback is the same request with an older tested revision.
The device-adapters worker picks the job up, so the HTTP request has already answered 202.
The job sends adapter-manager the decoder, the source with its secrets, the profile, the platform broker credentials and the bindings of devices already activated.
adapter-manager starts the tenant's containers if needed, replaces the adapter's flow and reads it back. Only a confirmed revision makes the adapter running.
If the manager refuses, cannot be reached or the job times out, the operation and the adapter are marked failed. The saved revision stays and nothing retries by itself.
The new flow's publisher connects to the platform broker and announces the edge node and every source it already knew.
Each source appears twice in Laravel: as the adapter's candidate with a decoded preview, and as a Discovery candidate holding the birth's metrics.
A person activates a source. Laravel creates the installation, maps the profile's parameters to the metrics of the same name and requests the device's activation.
The activation carries the source's stored birth. The runtime prefers a live birth, falls back to the stored one for an adapter-fed source, and records the applied generation.
The same revision is deployed again with the new binding. Until then the publisher sends only births for that source; afterwards it sends data stamped with the installation.
If a later decoder change announces different metrics, the device goes into review and its readings stop until a birth fits again or a new configuration is activated.
